content.alt: The Gingerbread Man - What kind of story is it?
content.text:
What kind of story is The Gingerbread Man?

The Gingerbread Man is a lively folktale about a gingerbread cookie that comes to life fresh out of the oven and runs off shouting, "Catch me if you can!" With its repeating refrain and chase structure, children can join in and shout along.

content.alt: The Gingerbread Man - The original story
content.text:
The original story of The Gingerbread Man

A widely known folktale (The Gingerbread Man) across the English-speaking world, it first appeared in print in an American magazine in 1875. The key is the repeating refrain, "Run, run, as fast as you can, you can't catch me, I'm the Gingerbread Man!" and in the end he's tricked and eaten by a clever fox — a warning against pride and deceit.
content.caption: The end of the chase

content.text:
Plot summary of The Gingerbread Man

When the gingerbread man an old woman baked comes to life and runs away, the old woman, the old man, and various animals chase after him, but no one can catch him. The overconfident gingerbread man, trying to cross a river, falls for the coaxing of a fox pretending to be kind, and in the end he's caught by the fox after all.

content.alt: The Gingerbread Man - The lesson it teaches
content.text:
The lesson The Gingerbread Man teaches

The heart of the story is that pride leads to carelessness, and you should be careful of a stranger who approaches with sweet words. Talk with your child about "when to be careful even if someone seems kind" and connect it to safety awareness.
content.caption: Watch out for trickery

content.alt: The Gingerbread Man - How to read it aloud
content.text:
How to read it aloud to your child

Shout the refrain "Run, run, you can't catch me!" together with your child, reading faster and faster. When the fox approaches, ask "Should we believe what the fox says?" to build discernment. It's well suited to ages 3-6.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. What age is The Gingerbread Man best for?
A. It's well suited to ages 3-6. The repeating refrain and chase structure are especially fun for younger children.

Q. Isn't the ending sad?
A. He does get eaten in the end, but it's drawn comically so it isn't heavy, and it naturally leads into the lesson of being wary of pride and trickery.

Q. What activities pair well with it?
A. Chanting the refrain together, baking and decorating gingerbread cookies, and a safety chat about "what if a stranger talks to you kindly?" are all great.
